s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of altered mental status, fever, flaccid paralysis, and respiratory failure with evidence of disseminated infection and multi-organ involvement
key_facts: Patient is around 60 years old
Patient lives in a rural area in the southeastern US
Patient has a history of porphyria with polyneuropathy
Patient has a history of alcohol use disorder
Patient has a recent diagnosis of hyper-IgE syndrome
Patient was taking oral prednisone before admission
Patient presented with fever
Patient has respiratory failure with lower lobe nodules and a left lower lobe infiltrate
Bronchoalveolar lavage revealed Aspergillus fumigatus, Candida spp, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa
Autopsy findings showed disseminated aspergillosis and candidiasis
Multiple organ involvement including lungs, liver, pancreas, colon, appendix, and kidneys

shortlist.label: Disseminated aspergillosis
shortlist.why_kept: Autopsy findings showed disseminated aspergillosis and patient had Aspergillus fumigatus in bronchoalveolar lavage

shortlist.label: Disseminated candidiasis
shortlist.why_kept: Autopsy findings showed disseminated candidiasis and patient had Candida spp in bronchoalveolar lavage

shortlist.label: Strongyloidiasis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has history of immunosuppression with oral prednisone and presented with altered mental status, fever, and flaccid paralysis

shortlist.label: Toxocariasis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient lives in a rural area and presented with eosinophil-rich inflammatory infiltrate in choroid, suggestive of parasitic infection

shortlist.label: Baylisascariasis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient lives in a rural area and presented with altered mental status, fever, and flaccid paralysis, consistent with baylisascariasis

raw.rationale: The presence of larval sections in the eye and the patient's immunocompromised state due to hyper-IgE syndrome and prednisone use, along with the eosinophil-rich inflammatory infiltrate, are key indicators of strongyloidiasis, which is also consistent with the patient's rural residence in the southeastern US where the parasite is more common.

rejected.label: Disseminated aspergillosis
rejected.why: While aspergillosis is present, it does not fully explain the larval sections found in the eye.

rejected.label: Disseminated candidiasis
rejected.why: Candidiasis does not account for the larval sections or the specific type of inflammatory infiltrate seen in the eyes.

rejected.label: Toxocariasis
rejected.why: Toxocariasis typically presents with visceral larva migrans or ocular larva migrans but does not usually cause the widespread organ involvement seen in this case.

rejected.label: Baylisascariasis
rejected.why: Baylisascariasis can cause similar symptoms but is less common in the southeastern US and typically associated with contact with raccoons, which is not mentioned in the case.
